Research

From dissertation to doctoral vision

Two stages of one question — whether integrating unconventional variables with modern machine learning genuinely improves how we forecast complex systems. Both are live, working proposals rather than finished conclusions.

In progress MSc Dissertation

Enhancing Financial Market Forecasting Using Lunar Cycles, Investor Sentiment, and Macroeconomic Indicators

Queen's University Belfast · GIFT City Campus · 2000–2025 S&P 500 study

Investigating whether lunar-phase data, investor sentiment (CNN Fear & Greed Index) and macroeconomic indicators add measurable predictive value to daily S&P 500 return forecasts, benchmarking regression and ARIMA against Random Forest, XGBoost and LSTM architectures. Feasibility work and exploratory analysis are complete; model development and evaluation are ongoing.

Status note: this is a live research project. Results referenced here reflect current direction, not final findings.

Word count ~8,173

Proposed Doctoral Research Vision

Cosmo-Statistical Intelligence: Forecasting Market Dynamics, Economic Cycles, and Environmental Change through Astronomical Knowledge and Machine Learning

FORESIGHTERS Doctoral Training Programme · Technology Theme

An extension of the dissertation's core question to a longer horizon: do planetary positions, conjunctions and transits documented in astronomical traditions carry statistically significant, falsifiable predictive information — for markets, economic cycles, human behaviour, and environmental anomalies — once tested against modern time-series and causal-inference methods. Every hypothesis is designed to be operationalised as a testable statistical proposition before any model is trained.

Status note: this is a proposal and future research direction — not a completed study or a claim of proven results.

Future Vision

Why I'm building this

My conviction is that ancient observational traditions and modern computational science are not opposites — they are two instruments pointed at the same long-horizon question, and I believe the statistical patterns I'm beginning to see in my dissertation work point toward something worth pursuing rigorously, all the way through to proof.

— on the motivation behind moving from dissertation to doctoral proposal

This is an ambition I hold as a responsibility rather than a claim: every hypothesis here is designed to be tested, falsifiable, and open to being wrong. The work is ongoing, and what's presented on this page is the direction of travel — not a finished result.
